title: Latency Tale: Causal-Chain Correlator for Burst SLO Violations and Adaptive Paging
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Background: We continue to see short-lived, high-severity SLO breaches (burst latency spikes) that cascade across service boundaries and generate noisy pages. Current burn-rate alerts and single-signal thresholds lack the context to attribute root cause, causing oncall thrash and delayed mitigation.

Objective: Build a lightweight Causal-Chain Correlator (CCC) that consumes tracing hooks, metrics and logs to: (1) correlate short-window SLO breaches across services, (2) infer likely causal chains (downstream amplification vs upstream regression), and (3) emit an enriched incident signal used to apply adaptive paging dampening and prioritized burn-rate escalation.

Success metrics: 
- Reduce paging noise during burst SLOs by 45% within first month of rollout (measured by pages per 7-day moving window for affected services).
- Median time-to-assign for correlated incidents improves by 25%.
- Precision of top-1 causal attribution >= 70% on annotated replay dataset.

Scope & approach: 
1) Ingest: wire CCC to existing tracing hooks (span sampling at 1-5% + on-error tail-sampling) and metrics/log pipeline (prometheus histograms, p50/p95/p99, and structured error logs).
2) Feature extraction: compute short-window delta metrics (30s, 2m), cross-service request fan-out ratios, and error co-occurrence rates.
3) Correlation model: lightweight rule-based + ML hybrid that (a) detects temporal precedence (service A latency spike precedes B by N ms), (b) flags amplification patterns (small upstream error -> large downstream latency), and (c) uses anomaly scores to suppress weak correlations.
4) Output: a structured incident enrichment payload (top-3 suspected causal links, confidence scores, relevant spans/trace IDs, implicated routes). Payload will be sent to the alerting layer to control paging dampening policies and to populate a dedicated SLO incident dashboard.

Rollout plan: Canary in staging with synthetic burst scenarios -> beta with 3 low-risk prod services -> opt-in for platform teams -> global enforcement.

Risks & trade-offs: 
- Additional processing increases pipeline cost and latency for enrichment; mitigate with sampling and time-bounded lookback.
- Attribution will be probabilistic; must avoid suppressing pages for true incidents. Initial policy will dampen paging (reduce page frequency or require secondary confirmation) rather than block pages entirely.

Deliverables: 
- CCC service and adapters for tracing/metrics/logs.
- A new incident enrichment API and an alerting policy extension for adaptive dampening.
- SLO incident dashboard (latency timelines, causal graph, representative traces).
- Evaluation harness and replay dataset for model tuning.
